proposal.diagnosis: All three trials remained upright but settled into double support with essentially zero forward speed. Preserve standing feedback while adding command-dependent forward ankle drive and opposing roll-responsive hip/knee motion to initiate unloading and forward swing. Ankle compensation approximately preserves swing-foot pitch; sustained alternation remains unverified.

r01 produced no steps: roll-driven leg differences decayed toward zero while forward drive moved the pelvis beyond stationary feet; seed 271 instead remained ankle-saturated and collapsed backward. Reduce command drive, strengthen opposing leg clearance, and reverse the roll-rate contribution to test sustained weight transfer rather than rapid damping. Retain the remaining r01 feedback.

r02's strong negative roll-rate feedback rapidly extended the support leg, launched the pelvis, and lost both contacts by 0.24 s. Recorded alternations occurred during collapse, not sustained walking. Sharply reduce that excitation and bound opposing leg excursions, with matching ankle compensation. Retain r02's reduced forward command drive to test gentler unloading.

r03 reduced launching and produced isolated touchdowns, but advancing either foot drove both ankle targets into negative saturation and both hips toward flexion as the pelvis retreated. Reduce this shared foot-position feedback fourfold to limit swing-to-stance interference and backward collapse. Retain r03's alternating leg coupling and command drive.

r04 still developed growing roll excursions, backward motion, and negative ankle saturation; weaker foot-position feedback alone did not repair this. Replace negative roll-rate damping with modest positive damping and reduce ankle self-following, approximately preserving ankle output at the reset angle. Retain command drive and opposing leg motion to test controlled stepping rather than collapse-associated touchdowns.

r05 suppressed the growing roll oscillation but also eliminated touchdowns; the pelvis then diverged forward or backward over stationary feet. Add lateral-velocity input to sustain weight transfer without restoring strong negative roll-rate feedback. Add sagittal velocity-dependent hip placement to oppose excessive forward reach during retreat and encourage forward placement during advance. Retain all other r05 coefficients.

r06 produced backward collapse in all seeds and only one isolated touchdown; the added sagittal hip-velocity term did not help. Remove that term and introduce a modest command-dependent hip-extension offset to test forward pelvis advancement over support. Retain the lateral-state coupling and opposing swing motion, without increasing ankle drive into existing saturation.

r07's hip offset did not prevent backward collapse; both ankle outputs again saturated negatively before useful alternation. Replace the unbounded shared ankle correction with a bounded tanh contribution, approximately retaining its small-signal gains. This tests whether preserving ankle adjustment range allows the retained weight-transfer and swing couplings to produce recoverable steps.

r08 reduced early ankle saturation but accelerated backward collapse, so saturation alone was not the cause. The positive hip command offset also produced backward pitch rather than sustained advancement. Reverse that offset modestly, test hip-velocity feedback opposite to the unsuccessful r06 sign, and increase bounded ankle authority. Retain the alternating leg coupling.

r09 kept the torso relatively upright during backward collapse but did not recover support beneath the pelvis. Negative velocity commanded further hip flexion, while forward foot displacement also increased flexion. Remove that velocity term and replace shared foot feedback with positive own-foot feedback to limit excessive forward reach and test foot retraction. Retain command-dependent alternating leg motion.

r10 still collapsed backward with no touchdowns; own-foot feedback did not establish a support exchange. Add contact asymmetry to reinforce flexion and forward swing of the unloaded leg while the opposite foot supports. The contribution cancels in double support, retaining existing roll-based initiation and reversal. This tests sustained swing clearance without restoring the destabilizing negative roll-rate feedback.

r11 initiated earlier touchdowns, but contact reinforcement produced abrupt exchanges, 0.32–0.36 m foot advances, and faster backward collapse. Reduce contact reinforcement while retaining its unloading cue, and add hip-joint velocity damping to limit swing overshoot and landing transients. Keep the remaining r11 coefficients unchanged.

r12 introduced large hip-target reversals, roughly +0.36 to -0.62, alongside contact-force spikes and early collapse. Replace raw hip-velocity damping with a gentler bounded contribution so it cannot overwhelm swing targets. Retain the reduced contact reinforcement and all other r12 coefficients; sustained alternation remains absent.

r13 reduced hip-target reversals, but support exchanges remained ineffective and backward collapse persisted. Replace symmetric knee flexion/extension with flexion-biased nonlinear responses: preserve the neutral knee target at 0.50 m/s while limiting support-leg extension and retaining swing flexion. This tests unloading without the support-leg lengthening seen during unsuccessful exchanges.

r14 extended upright duration in seeds 272/273, but neither established alternating steps before sagittal divergence. Increase knee sensitivity to weight transfer while retaining its limited support-extension range. Update ankle compensation to match the nonlinear knee targets and existing hip swing, approximately preserving neutral output and swing-foot pitch.

r15 produced only right-foot touchdowns, including two consecutive ones in seed 272, before backward collapse. Add reciprocal foot-separation feedback to favor lifting and advancing the trailing leg, then release that drive as it passes the other foot. Modestly increase forward-command ankle drive while retaining its bounded response and the current knee/ankle coordination.

r16 increased initial forward motion in seeds 272/273 but produced no touchdowns; the pelvis still escaped stationary support. Add a modest command-dependent left-swing preference to initiate a clearer unloading event. Retain reciprocal foot-separation feedback so advancing the left foot can favor the right leg next. This is a fixed state-dependent bias, not a timed phase.

r17 produced a three-touchdown alternating run in seed 273, but only during backward retreat; all seeds still collapsed backward. Retain that exchange mechanism and test a stronger command-dependent forward-pitch preference with increased pitch feedback, rather than further increasing swing amplitude. The earlier positive hip-command offset produced backward pitch.

r18 shifted early torso pitch forward but did not stop backward pelvis drift or establish alternation. During retreat, ankle angles increased and positive angle feedback weakened the negative corrective target. Replace ankle self-following with restoring feedback, preserving output at the -0.4 rad reset angle. Retain the current command drive and leg-exchange mechanism.

r19 still produced isolated or repeated same-foot touchdowns, not sustained support exchanges; ankle stiffening did not resolve backward collapse. Add bounded hip-roll coupling synchronized with the existing swing signal to test shifting weight toward the supporting leg during unloading. Retain r19's sagittal feedback, knee shaping, and ankle coordination.

r20 produced forward travel in seeds 272/273, but no touchdowns: the pelvis advanced beyond stationary feet. Retain its weight-transfer coupling and add command-dependent left-knee flexion to test earlier unloading, with matching ankle compensation to approximately preserve foot pitch. Existing reciprocal state feedback remains responsible for subsequent exchanges.

r21's added left-knee flexion lowered the pelvis without lifting the foot; left support remained substantial, often exceeding right support. Add a command-dependent lateral hip-roll offset to test shifting load toward the right foot so existing left-leg shortening can create clearance. Retain the reciprocal feedback for subsequent support exchange.

r22 produced zero touchdowns. At 0.1 s, left/right support forces were 332/57 N and 367/47 N in seeds 272/273. Reverse the lateral offset to test unloading the flexed left leg; retain all other coefficients.

r23 briefly unloaded the left foot in seeds 272/273, but lateral velocity reached 0.22–0.23 m/s before sustained left loading returned. Increase lateral-velocity feedback to test braking that overshoot while retaining the initial unloading offset and all other r23 coefficients.

r24 reduced lateral drift but left-foot unloading in seeds 272/273 ended before 0.24 s, with zero qualifying touchdowns. Moderately strengthen contact-dependent knee flexion and its existing ankle compensation to test sustained swing clearance. Keep hip-swing feedback and lateral damping unchanged.

r25 increased initial left-foot clearance, but contact returned by 0.24 s with zero qualifying touchdowns. Negative roll coincided with rapidly reduced left-knee flexion commands. Reduce roll sensitivity in the knee/ankle phase units to test maintaining clearance longer; retain all other r25 coefficients.

r26 retained sustained left loading and increased lateral drift; its sole qualifying touchdown was right-sided, late in the fall. Halve tonic left-knee flexion and its ankle compensation to test reducing persistent leg asymmetry while preserving contact-dependent alternating flexion. Retain all other coefficients.

r27 still produced zero touchdowns and persistent leftward drift. Replace the tonic lateral offset with contact-dependent offsets: preserve its magnitude during right-only support, reverse it during left-only support, and cancel it during double support. Test support exchange without a permanent lateral bias; retain all other coefficients.

r28 reduced early lateral drift but still produced zero touchdowns and fore-aft falls over planted feet. Strengthen each hip's own-foot position feedback to test advancing trailing feet and retracting excessively forward feet. Retain all lateral, knee, and ankle coefficients from r28.

r29 still produced zero touchdowns: stronger foot-position feedback changed posture without establishing support exchange. Test a small roll-rate sign reversal across the reciprocal phase units to encourage alternating motion. Keep its magnitude far below the earlier destabilizing reversal and retain all other r29 coefficients.
